title: Foreign Issuers Flock To Euro Debt
gist: Non-resident issuance of euro-denominated debt hit a record €352bn in H1 2026, more than triple the 2021-24 first-half average of €108bn, yet European institutional demand absorbed it without strain. Gavekal reads the boom as deepening rather than crowding out the euro credit market, easing the shift of domestic borrowers from bank loans to capital markets.

insights.claim: Non-resident issuance of euro-denominated debt into the eurozone reached a record €352bn in the first half of 2026, up from €287bn in H1 2025 and more than triple the €108bn first-half average of 2021-24.
insights.speaker: August Gudmundsson
insights.so_what: A step-change in euro-denominated supply is a concrete marker of the euro's growing role as a global funding currency — watch euro credit supply calendars and cross-currency basis for follow-through.
insights.quote: In the first six months of 2026, non-residents issued a record €352bn, up from €287bn in the same period of 2025 and more than triple the first-half average for 2021-24 of €108bn.

insights.claim: Foreign borrowers are now tapping the euro market at an unprecedented rate, marking a structural break rather than a cyclical blip in euro-denominated funding by non-residents.
insights.speaker: August Gudmundsson
insights.so_what: If the shift is structural, it argues for persistent foreign demand for euro funding and a broader, more liquid euro credit universe to allocate into.
insights.quote: Non-residents are issuing more euro-denominated debt into the eurozone than ever before.

insights.claim: European institutional investors have queued up to buy high-quality euro assets, allowing the market to absorb record non-resident supply easily despite the sheer weight of issuance.
insights.speaker: August Gudmundsson
insights.so_what: Deep domestic bid means heavy supply need not widen euro credit spreads — a reason to fade 'indigestion' narratives around large euro issuance windows.
insights.quote: markets have absorbed the additional flow easily as European institutional investors have queued up to buy high-quality euro assets
insights.locator: Yet despite the weight of issuance

insights.claim: The surge in non-resident euro issuance is deepening the euro credit market and attracting additional capital rather than crowding out domestic borrowers.
insights.speaker: August Gudmundsson
insights.so_what: Cuts against the standard crowding-out worry: heavy foreign supply is a positive-sum liquidity event for euro credit, supportive of domestic issuers' access rather than a headwind.
insights.quote: Rather than crowding out domestic borrowers, the boom in non-resident issuance appears to be deepening the euro credit market, attracting additional capital
insights.locator: Rather than crowding out domestic borrowers

insights.claim: Deeper euro credit markets are making it easier for European domestic companies to continue their gradual shift away from bank lending towards capital markets financing.
insights.speaker: August Gudmundsson
insights.so_what: A slow disintermediation of European corporate funding is negative at the margin for eurozone bank loan growth and positive for debt capital markets franchises and euro corporate bond supply.
insights.quote: making it easier for domestic companies to continue their gradual shift towards capital markets financing
insights.locator: Rather than crowding out domestic borrowers
